q: 1. In "Full face" method of constructing tunnels, the first operation relates to
options: excavation of one drift in the centre
excavation being done along the periphery
explain: In the full-face tunnelling method, excavation typically begins along the periphery of the tunnel section before removing the central core material.

q: 2. Which one of the following is a component of a shield for tunnelling?
explain: A tunnelling shield's essential components include the cutting edge (which advances into the ground ahead of excavation), along with the hood and tail, distinguishing it from liner plates or trench jacks.

q: 3. Which one of the following statements is not correct for heading and benching method of tunnelling?
options: Drilling and mucking can be done simultaneously
Benching provides a plateform for working on heading
Removal of muck from the heading is very easy
explain: In the heading and benching method, mucking (removing debris) from the elevated heading portion is actually difficult (not easy) because of restricted working space and the need to lower material down, making this statement incorrect.

q: 4. The difference of heights of the tunnels above rail tops of BG and MG tracks is kept
explain: Per railway tunnelling standards, the extra headroom difference between Broad Gauge (BG) and Metre Gauge (MG) tunnel clearances above rail level is typically about 0.60 m.

q: 5. In case of drift method of tunnelling, the drift may be excavated at
explain: The pilot drift (small preliminary tunnel) in the drift method can be excavated at the centre, top (crown), or bottom (invert) of the section depending on ground conditions, so all locations are valid options.

q: 6. A tunnel is found more advantageous as compared to the alternate routes because it
options: reduces the cost by reducing the route distance and maintenance cost
explain: Tunnels offer multiple advantages simultaneously — protection from snow/weather, shorter route distance (lower operating/maintenance cost), and avoidance of surface right-of-way conflicts.

q: 7. Pick up the correct statement regarding drilling a tunnel from the following
options: Holes are drilled by pneumatically operated rock drills
One drill is required for each 4 to 5 m2 force area
The diameter of the bore hole at the deepest point should be 6 mm more than the diameter of the cartridge
explain: All three statements about tunnel drilling practice — pneumatic drills, drill spacing per face area, and borehole-to-cartridge diameter tolerance — are standard, correct practices.

q: 8. For tunnels exceeding 300 m in length, the grade should be provided below
explain: For long tunnels (>300 m), the design grade is restricted to about 75% of the ruling gradient to ensure safe train operation/ventilation within the tunnel.

q: 9. The method of draining in the tunnels, is generally known as
explain: Tunnel drainage encompasses foredrainage (before construction), dewatering (during construction), and permanent drainage systems (after completion) — all are part of overall tunnel drainage practice.

q: 10. Pick up the correct statement from the following during tunnel excavation
options: Oxygen should not be less than 19.5%
Carbondioxide should not be more than 0.5%
Hydrogen sulphide should not be more than 0.001%
explain: All these are recognized safe air-quality limits (oxygen minimum, CO2 maximum, H2S maximum) mandated for worker safety during tunnel excavation.

q: 11. To attain the required shape of the tunnel section, we use
explain: Trimmer holes are drilled around the perimeter of the tunnel face and fired last to trim the section to its exact required shape and profile.

q: 12. The most commonly adopted pattern of cut holes is
explain: Various cut-hole patterns — horizontal wedge, pyramid, fan, and V-cut — are all commonly used in tunnel blasting, chosen based on rock type and tunnel section.

q: 13. Which one of the following linings is suitable for shield driven tunnels particularly in the subaqueous regions :
explain: Cast iron segmental lining is preferred for shield-driven tunnels beneath water bodies (subaqueous) because it provides high strength and excellent watertightness against high external water pressure.

q: 14. Pick up the mechanical ventilation method used for tunnels from the following
options: blowing fresh air by ducts to the face of tunnel
exhausting foul air by ducts from the face of the tunnel and permitting fresh air through the tunnel
blowing fresh air and exhausting foul air by ducts
explain: Mechanical tunnel ventilation can use blowing (supply), exhausting (extraction), or combined blowing-and-exhausting systems — all are recognized ventilation strategies.

q: 15. Which one of the following methods of tunnelling does not require the use of time bearing
explain: According to the reference book, none of the listed methods (liner plate, shield, compressed air) require timbering support, as they use other structural support systems instead.

q: 16. For highways, tunnelling is preferred to if the open cut exceeds :
explain: For highway alignments, tunnelling becomes economically preferable over deep open cutting once the cut depth exceeds about 15 m (theoretically up to about 18 m), beyond which cutting costs escalate.

q: 17. Which one of the following statements is not correct in respect of setting of an inclined tunnel:
options: Reference points are constructed on the roof of tunnels
The alignment is fixed from upper/lower apex point.
The level of the invert at the heading is marked by a tape.
explain: According to the book's answer key, all three statements about setting out an inclined tunnel (roof reference points, apex-based alignment, invert level marking) are correct, so 'none of the above' is the right choice.

q: 18. Forepoling method is generally adopted for tunnelling in :
explain: Forepoling (driving poling boards/plates ahead of excavation) is a supporting technique specifically used in soft, unstable ground to prevent roof collapse ahead of the face.

q: 19. Concrete lining is provided concurrently with the driving operation in case of
explain: In hard/rock terrain, concrete lining can be placed concurrently with excavation advance since the rock itself is stable enough to remain open temporarily without immediate support.

q: 20. The concentration of the dust particles of the size 0.5 to 5 microns adjacent to the working face should not be more than
explain: Safety standards for tunnel excavation limit the respirable dust concentration (0.5-5 micron particles) near the working face to not more than 400 particles per cm³, to protect worker health.

q: 21. Which one of the following statements is not correct with regard to heading and benching method of tunnelling.
options: Driving of tunnel is done in two portions of its section
Driving the top portion is done in advance of the bottom portion
After driving the top portion 3 m to 3.5 m holes are drilled into the head and bench
Firing of head holes is done just before the bench holes are fired
explain: In practice, the bench holes are fired first (or with adequate free face preparation), and head holes are fired appropriately timed relative to that — not simply 'just before' as stated, making this the incorrect statement.

q: 22. Which one of the following methods is generally used for the layout of the muck-car tracks
options: the cherry picker, California crossing, Dixon conveyor
explain: Multiple layout methods (grasshopper, passing track, cherry picker/California crossing, Dixon conveyor) are all recognized techniques for arranging muck-car tracks in tunnel construction.

q: 23. For full face method, the excavation to be done is generally divided into
explain: In the full-face tunnelling method, the face is typically divided into three sections (e.g., top, middle, bottom) to systematize excavation and support work.

q: 24. The tunnels, the artificial underground passages are constructed for :
explain: Tunnels serve a wide range of purposes including highways, railways, and water supply/sewerage conveyance — all valid applications.

q: 25. In the wooded bulk-head, used for mucking in steep grade tunnels,
explain: A wooden bulkhead used for controlling muck flow in steep-grade tunnels is typically constructed with two openings to manage material discharge.

q: 26. Railway tunnels, are generally
explain: Railway tunnel cross-sections are commonly designed with a polycentric (multi-centred curved) profile to efficiently accommodate the loading gauge and structural stability requirements.

q: 27. Pick up the explosive used for tunnelling in soft rocks from the following
explain: Ammonia dynamite, being a lower-strength explosive, is suitable for controlled blasting in softer rock formations where excessive shattering must be avoided.

q: 28. Which one of the following methods is generally adopted for tunnelling in firm ground
explain: In firm, self-supporting ground, multiple tunnelling methods (full face, heading and benching, drift) can all be successfully employed since the ground itself provides adequate temporary stability.

q: 29. An overhead track on a large truss frame is required in case of car changer by
explain: The grasshopper method for muck-car changing uses an overhead track supported on a large truss frame to shift empty/loaded cars past each other.

q: 30. The length of the needle beam used in needle beam method of tunnelling is usually
explain: In the needle beam method of tunnel support, the needle beams used to temporarily support the crown while excavating below are typically about 5 m to 6 m in length.

q: 31. For hauling muck from the tunnel, the following type of muck-car is used
explain: Various muck-car types (muck box, ballast-ship type, side dump, U-bottom cars) are all used in practice for hauling excavated material out of a tunnel.

q: 32. Which one of the following methods is adopted for permanent drainage of tunnels :
explain: Permanent tunnel drainage relies on a combination of longitudinal drains, continuous open drains, and impermeable concrete lining with grouting — all methods work together for long-term water management.

q: 33. The underground routes or passages driven through the ground without disturbing overlying soil cover are called
explain: By definition, a tunnel is an underground passage constructed through the ground without disturbing the overlying soil/rock cover, distinguishing it from open-cut excavation.

q: 34. Type of tunnels which are excavated to divert the traffic load of whatsoever type from surface to subsurface routes.
explain: Traffic tunnels are specifically constructed to carry surface transportation (roads, railways, pedestrians) onto subsurface alignments, diverting traffic load underground.

q: 35. Pick the tunnel which is not a sub-group of traffic tunnels.
explain: Sewage tunnels fall under public utility tunnels (for conveying wastewater), not under traffic tunnels, which cover railway, highway, and pedestrian passages.

q: 36. Tunnels associated with hydropower generation are called
explain: Tunnels built specifically to convey water for electricity generation at hydroelectric projects are termed hydropower tunnels.

q: 37. Circular section of tunnels is not suitable for
explain: A circular section, while structurally efficient for water conveyance and shield-driven tunnels in loose ground, is comparatively less convenient for placing/forming concrete lining uniformly compared to other shapes.

q: 38. A good blast with a good yield is obtained if the cut hole is
explain: Cut holes angled at about 45° to the tunnel face create an effective wedge/relief for the main blast, producing a good yield compared to holes drilled normal to the face.

q: 39. In 'N' is the number of shafts used, then the total number of faces available for attacking the excavation and construction in tunnels are
explain: Each shaft provides two working faces (one in each direction along the tunnel), plus the two natural end faces (portals) of the tunnel, giving a total of 2N+2 faces.

q: 40. In compressed air tunneling, the volume of free air provided is
options: 6m3 per second per m2 of face area
6m3 per minute per m2 of face area
20m3 per minute per m2 of face area
6m3 per hour per m2 of face area
explain: Standard practice for compressed air tunnelling specifies a fresh air supply rate of about 6 cubic metres per minute for each square metre of tunnel face area, ensuring adequate ventilation for workers.

q: 41. If 'D' is the diameter of tunnel in meters then the thickness of lining in mm, as pe the empirical formula is given by
explain: A commonly cited empirical formula for tunnel lining thickness (in mm) is approximately t = 82D, where D is the tunnel diameter in metres.

q: 42. Ribs are use for strengthening and stiffening the liner plate for tunnels of diameter greater than
explain: For larger tunnels (diameter exceeding about 3 m), additional steel ribs are used to reinforce and stiffen the liner plates against ground pressure, since the plates alone become insufficient beyond this size.

q: 43. The most suitable soil for compresses air tunneling is
explain: Compressed air tunnelling works best in soft, saturated clay and silty ground because the applied air pressure effectively balances groundwater pressure and stabilizes the face, unlike highly permeable sand/gravel where air would simply escape.

q: 44. Which of the following methods of tunnelling is used for long tunnels at great depths?
explain: The Austrian (New Austrian Tunnelling Method-related) approach is generally adopted for long, deep tunnels where ground support sequencing and rock mass behaviour are critical.

q: 45. The line at which the tunnel wall breaks from sloping outward can be given as
explain: The spring line marks the point on a tunnel's cross-section where the curved arch/roof portion transitions to the vertical (or sloping) side walls.

q: 46. Which of the following should be considered while aligning a tunnel?
explain: Hydrological conditions (groundwater table, seepage, water-bearing strata) critically affect tunnel alignment decisions, more so than atmospheric or climatic factors at the surface.

q: 47. Which method can be adopted if full face excavation is not possible?
explain: When the full tunnel face cannot be excavated at once (due to size or ground conditions), the heading and benching method — excavating the section in stages — is adopted instead.

q: 48. Tunneling is required in case of .............
explain: Tunneling is specifically employed to create an underground passage, distinct from surface construction.

q: 49. The most suitable soil for compressed air tunneling is .............
explain: Per the reference key, silt is marked as most suitable for compressed air tunneling in this classification.

q: 50. In a compressed air tunneling, the volume of free air provided is .............
options: 6 m3 per second per m2 of face area
6 m3 per minute per m2 of face area
20 m3 per minute per m2 of face area
6 m3 per hour per m2 of face area
explain: Standard practice for compressed air tunneling supplies free air at a rate of about 6 m3 per minute per m2 of tunnel face area.
